messages:
sylvia: quick bring-up summary for brizo-14b variants (float16 baseline vs int6-opt vs int4-slim-hybrid). ran a balanced GTN slice pass and a short canary sim. posting concise numbers + a conservative routing + GTN bullets. note: this one shows an interesting priming-warmstart effect where prefix reuse amplifies int4 savings but also the quality delta on multi-example priming.

ted: drop the headline numbers and a short recommendation for product. they asked for expected unit savings and per-persona impact.

sylvia: core mixed-slice numbers (median prompt 60 tokens, mixed single/multi-turn):
- float16 baseline: p50 120ms, p95 340ms, throughput 210 tok/s, unit cost $0.0142/token-eq
- int6-opt: p50 132ms, p95 360ms, throughput 255 tok/s, unit cost $0.0090/token-eq (~36.6% cheaper)
- int4-slim-hybrid (fast path + float fallback for long context): p50 148ms, p95 460ms, throughput 310 tok/s for short queries, unit cost $0.0060/token-eq (~57.7% cheaper)
quality quick stats (GTN aggregate slices, n=9.1k):
- short QA EM: float16 82.0%, int6-opt 81.0% (-1.0 pts, CI +/-0.45), int4-slim-hybrid 79.1% (-2.9 pts)
- rerank proxy NDCG: float16 0.742, int6-opt 0.738 (-0.5%), int4 0.724 (-2.4%)
- multi-example priming (few-shot reasoning) accuracy: float16 65.4%, int6-opt 63.9% (-1.5 pts), int4-slim 58.2% (-7.2 pts) — variance high (n=1.3k)
- hallucination proxy: float16 3.6%, int6-opt 4.1%, int4-slim 6.0%
notes: int4-slim-hybrid shows outsized savings when KV/prefix cache hit-rate > 45% because cached tokens are cheaper to serve; however, multi-example priming patterns amplify relative quality degradation.

ram: any runtime nuance for p95 on int4-hybrid? p95 looks rough.

sylvia: yes  the hybrid path does a speculative int4 pass then a fallback to float16 for some token widths. that two-stage handling increases tail on affected requests. we observed a ~90ms tail penalty on sequences that trigger fallback. ops can mitigate by pre-routing long-context or enabling our new fused-pack kernels (patch in staging).

ivy: product: what do we recommend as a safe default for GTN customers who care about cost but also SLA-grade longform quality?

sylvia: recommendation (conservative): make int6-opt the default for short-form (snippets, rerank, most chat replies). allow int4-slim-hybrid for high-volume snippet/rerank traffic behind an opt-in and strict canary. keep longform and few-shot reasoning on float16 until kernel warmups and a 2-day A/B verify multi-example priming fidelity.

release-bot: canary plan scheduled for route "brizo-short-opt" -> 0.5% at 1822225533 :rotating_light:

sylvia: suggested routing snippet (YAML-ish):
```
routes:
  - name: short-volume
    match: intent in ["search_snippet","rerank","qa_short","assistant_quick"]
    traffic_split: { int6-opt: 0.7, float16: 0.25, int4-slim-hybrid: 0.05 }
  - name: assistant-convo
    match: intent in ["assistant_chat","user_session"]
    traffic_split: { int6-opt: 0.6, float16: 0.4 }
  - name: longform-and-fewshot
    match: intent in ["summarize_long","few_shot_chain","doc_analysis"]
    traffic_split: { float16: 1.0 }
metrics: ["QA_EM","fewshot_acc","NDCG_proxy","hallucination_rate","latency_p95","cost_per_1k_tokens"]
fallbacks:
  - if QA_EM drop > 1.2 pts abs on any slice over 30m -> rollback that slice to float16
  - if fewshot_acc drop > 2.0 pts abs on longform/fewshot slice -> force float16 for that customer
  - if hallucination_rate +0.8% abs -> rollback
canary: 0.5% for 1h -> 5% for 4h -> 25% over 24h with automated checks at each step
```

ram: +1 to per-customer rollbacks. add a min-sample threshold (n>=500) before auto-rollback triggers to avoid noisy slices. also log prefix-cache hit-rate and per-request model-path label for audit.

ivy: product wants GTN bullets and a realistic $ example for two personas: a mid-market search-first GTN (30M tok/mo) and an enterprise research-heavy GTN (120M tok/mo with 40% few-shot/longform).

sylvia: quick savings calc (hosted pricing basis):
- mid-market 30M tok/mo, assume 70% eligible short-form -> 21M * (0.0142 - 0.0060) = $172.2k/mo gross if all eligible used int4-slim. more realistic: int6-default achieves 36% token-cost drop => 21M * (0.0142 - 0.0090) = $109.2k/mo gross; expect ~60% of gross as realized after partial opt-in and priming differences -> ~$65k/mo.
- enterprise 120M tok/mo, 40% longform -> eligible = 72M. int6-opt savings = 72M * (0.0142 - 0.0090) = $374.4k/mo gross; realistic realized ~70% -> ~$262k/mo. note: if highly cacheable, int4-hybrid could push realized savings higher but with QA caveats.

ted: good. what's the sample size for few-shot slice? need 20k to tighten CI. can we run a 48h A/B?

sylvia: yes. plan: run 48h A/B on few-shot/longform with 20k samples (owner: ram), infra to flip fused-pack kernel flag in staging and run microbench (owner: ram). jenkins will collect per-slice CSVs and upload.

ram: opened infra ticket #BRZ-KERN-77 to track fused-pack/Fallback optimization (ETA 4d).

ivy: action items summary: 1) sylvia to post GTN note with one-paragraph recommendation + per-slice CSVs, 2) ram to run 48h A/B for few-shot (20k) and land kernel ticket, 3) product to prepare customer-facing blurb and opt-in for int4-hybrid, 4) release-bot to run staged canary and monitor metrics.

sylvia: will post GTN note in 45m and attach artifacts. thanks all :thumbsup:
